L734: ## 17.1.2. Phase 1 Studies Not Included in the Original NDA Submissions
L735: The following phase 1 studies were not included in the original NDA submissions or the previous NDA 90-day safety update report. The provided information is based on the NDA resubmission safety update data cut date.
L736: ## 17.1.2.1. Study 4540
L737: Study 4540 is an ongoing, phase 1, open-label study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK), safety, and tolerability of SC LEN in healthy adult subjects, who received a single dose of SC LEN (927 mg as the sodium salt) on Day 1, administered into alternative injection sites (thigh [Cohort 1] and upper arm [Cohort 2]) in comparison with the abdomen (Cohort 3) as the reference site. A total of 30 subjects was enrolled in the study, 10 in each of Cohorts 1, 2, and 3, all of whom received a single dose (927 mg) of SC LEN.
L738: ## 17.1.2.2. Study 5710
L739: Study 5710 is an ongoing, phase 1, open-label, multiple-cohort study to evaluate the PK, safety, and tolerability of single doses of SC and intramuscular (IM) LEN formulations containing different concentrations of both LEN and [REDACTED](b) (4), administered to healthy adult subjects, with or without an optional oral LEN loading dose as determined prior to cohort initiation based on available data. Dose escalation through cohorts was performed in an adaptive manner. A total of 98 subjects was enrolled in Cohorts 1 (1200 mg; n=22), 3 (300 mg; n=21), 4
L740: NDA 215973 Sunlenca (lenacapavir) injection, for subcutaneous use
NDA 215974 Sunlenca (lenacapavir) tablets, for oral use
L741: (100 mg; n=12), 7 (125 mg; n=11), 10 (150 mg; n=12), and 13 (300 mg; n=20), and each had received the protocol-specified single SC LEN injection on Day 1, with doses ranging from 100 to 1200 mg containing up to (b) (4). No optional oral loading dose was required to be administered to subjects in Cohort 1, 3, 4, 7, or 10, whereas subjects in Cohort 13 were administered a protocol-required 600 mg oral LEN loading dose on Days 1 and 2. All subjects in the specified cohorts completed study drug and there were no premature study drug discontinuations due to an adverse event (AE). Not all cohorts had enrolled.
L742: ## 17.1.2.3. Study 5717
L743: Study 5717 is an ongoing, phase 1, open-label, multiple-cohort study to evaluate the PK, safety, and tolerability of single doses of SC or IM LEN formulations containing different concentrations of both LEN and (b) (4), administered to healthy adult subjects, with or without an optional oral LEN loading dose for subjects receiving an IM LEN injection, depending on cohort and based upon available data. A total of 57 subjects had been enrolled variously in Cohorts 1 (2400 mg; n=20), 2 (2400 mg; n=10), 4 (3200 mg; n=10), 6 (2400 mg; n=7), and 11 (2400 mg; n=10). Subjects in Cohorts 1, 2, 4, and 6 had received the protocol-specified single SC LEN injection on Day 1, with doses ranging from 2400 mg to 3200 mg, while subjects in Cohort 11 had received a single IM LEN injection on Day 1 with no protocol requirement for an optional oral loading dose. All subjects in the cohorts identified completed study drug, and there were no premature discontinuations from study drug because of an AE. Not all cohorts had enrolled.
L744: ## 17.1.2.4. Study 5977
L745: Study 5977 was a phase 1, open-label study to evaluate the PK, safety, and tolerability of oral LEN in healthy adult subjects, who received a single oral dose of LEN (25 mg) on Day 1 (Cohort 1), or multiple oral doses of LEN (25 mg) once daily for 56 days (Cohort 2). A total of 34 subjects was enrolled in the study, Cohort 1 (n=8) and Cohort 2 (n=26), all of whom received at least one dose of study drug. There were no discontinuations due to AEs.
L746: ## 17.1.2.5. Study 5816
L747: Study 5816 is an ongoing phase 1, randomized, blinded, proof-of-concept study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the broadly neutralizing antibodies GS-5423 and GS-2872 in combination with LEN in virologically suppressed adults with human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection. Subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio into one of two treatment groups, each of which received on Day 1 a loading dose of oral LEN 600 mg, followed by SC LEN 927 mg, followed by intravenous infusions of, first, GS-5423 30 mg/kg body weight, and, second, GS-2872 at a dose of 10 or 30 mg/kg depending on treatment group. A further loading dose of oral LEN 600 mg was administered on Day 2. A total of 21 subjects was randomized and received at least one dose of study drug. No subject discontinued study drug due to an AE.
L748: ## 17.1.2.6. Study 6148
L749: Study 6148 was a phase 1, open-label, parallel-design, single-dose, three-cohort study to evaluate the potential drug-drug interaction between islatravir (ISL) and LEN in healthy adult subjects who received coadministered oral ISL 20 mg and oral LEN 600 mg (Cohort 1), oral islatravir 20 mg (Cohort 2), or oral LEN 600 mg (Cohort 3) under fasted conditions on the morning of Day 1. A total of 55 subjects was enrolled in the study, 18 in each of Cohorts 1 and 2, and 19 in Cohort 3; each subject received their assigned single dose(s) of study drug. No subject prematurely discontinued study drug due to an AE.

L805: ## 17.4. Supplemental Data for the Safety Review: Injection Site Reactions
L806: ## 17.4.1. Resolved and Ongoing Injection Site Indurations and Injection Site Nodules by Study
L807: As requested by the Agency, the Applicant submitted a cumulative review of injection-site reactions (ISRs), including ongoing and resolved injection site nodules and indurations and general updates on all types of ISRs from LEN studies (as appropriate and feasible, that include SC dosing regardless of the specific formulation, dose or injection volume).
L808: ## **Study 4625: LEN-Related Injection Site Nodules and Indurations**
L809: Overall, 18 of 72 subjects (25.0%) experienced study drug-related injection site nodules, and 11 subjects (15.3%) experienced study drug-related injection site indurations; all events were Grade 1 or 2 in severity.
L810: The duration of nodules and indurations occurring as a result of the first SC LEN injections was longer than those occurring as a result of the second LEN SC injections (since their follow-up was longer) and longer for ongoing ones (compared to resolved ones).
L811: NDA 215973 Sunlenca (lenacapavir) injection, for subcutaneous use
NDA 215974 Sunlenca (lenacapavir) tablets, for oral use

As of June 15 2022, the Applicant had received dermatologist assessments for two subjects from Study 4625 who met the aforementioned ISR criteria; a summary of the biopsy reports is provided in Table 53.

L888: ## 17.4.3. Assessment of the Role of the Physical and Chemical Characteristics of Lenacapavir in ISRs
L889: The Applicant provided their assessment on the role of physical and chemical characteristics of LEN on ISRs; this included an assessment of nonclinical and clinical data for LEN and other antiretrovirals (ARVs). In summary, the Applicant states that their review of ISRs and pH for various SC ARVs as well as other LEN formulations did not identify a clear association between high pH of a formulation and ISRs. In addition, the Applicant believes that the ISRs observed in clinical studies with SC LEN, including nodules and indurations, are likely associated with the presence of a SC LEN depot.
L890: The Applicant states that their available nonclinical data suggest that chronic granulomatous inflammation and foreign body response at the SC injection site are expected to occur for an antiretroviral compound, including LEN, due to the presence of a SC drug depot, and irrespective of the pH of the formulation.
L891: *Clinical Reviewer's Comment: Based on the information provided, the review team agrees that the Applicant's conclusions are reasonable.*

L920: ## United States Prescribing Information Labeling Review
L921: ## Overview of Major Labeling Changes
L922: - Highlighted below are significant changes made to the prescribing information from the Applicant's proposed labeling submitted on June 28, 2021 for Sunlenca (lenacapavir).
- HIGHLIGHTS and TABLE OF CONTENTS were revised for consistency with the full Prescribing Information.
L923: ## 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE
L924: - The indications statement was modified (b) (4)
- The indication statement was modified (b) (4)
L925: Associated changes have also been made in Section (b) (4). Refer to Section (b) (4) of the previous, February 28, 2022 review.
L926: ## 2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION
L927: - The final approved labeling will include two options for initiation. Option 1, as initially proposed by the applicant; and Option 2, an 'oral' lead-in option, agreed to with the Applicant through the course of the review. Refer to Section 6.3.2. of the previous, February 28, 2022 review.
L928: - Instructions to inspect for particulates has been expanded to include inspection of the prepared syringe in addition to the drug vial. This addition added in consideration of the potential for particulates (b) (4).
L929: ## 3 CONTRAINDICATIONS
L930: - The contraindication initially proposed (b) (4) has been revised to contraindicate use with 'strong CYP3A inducers'. Refer to Section 8.2.2. of the previous, February 28, 2022 review.
L931: ## 4 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
L932: - A new Warnings and Precautions subsection has been added to discuss the long-acting properties and potential associated risks with SUNLENCA. This new subsection addresses the risk of viral resistance if not transitioned to alternative therapy as well as the potential for adverse reactions through interaction with sensitive CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic indices for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose. Refer to Section 6.2 of the previous, February 28, 2022 review.
- A new Warnings and Precautions subsection has been added to discuss the risk of injection site reactions (ISRs). This new subsection has been added in consideration of the long duration of nodules and indurations, relatively high incidence of ISRs and discontinuations seen as a result in the clinical studies. Refer to Section 7.7.2 of this review.
L933: ## 5 ADVERSE REACTIONS
L934: - Discussion has been added to Section 6.1 to discuss local injection site reactions. Refer to Section 7.7.2 of this review.
L935: ## 6 DRUG INTERACTIONS
L936: - A section regarding Narcotic Analgesic/Treatment of Opioid Dependence has been added to the drug interactions table.
L937: (b) (4)
L938: ## 7 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY
L939: - Exposure-response data have been added to Section 12.2.
- Information regarding In Vitro Studies of drug interactions was added.

L1033: ## **Observations and Results**
L1034: ## Mortality
L1035: Animals were checked twice daily for mortality and signs of pain or distress. The survival rates are presented in **Table 1**. The animal was found dead or sacrificed early due to its moribund condition were noted as the causes of death. The overall lowest survival rate (76%) was in males dosed with 100 mg/kg, whereas, in high dosed males (300 mg/kg), the survival rate was 92% which is similar to that seen in control males (96% survival). The higher incident of mortality in males at 100 mg/kg is unlikely related to the test article because the mortality incidence in males at 300 mg/kg was similar to controls and this effect was not seen in females.

L1040: ## Clinical Signs
L1041: Cageside observations were conducted once daily. Detailed observations were conducted at predose, prior to dosing on day 1, and weekly throughout the study.
L1042: Test article administration resulted injection site reactions of raised areas at dosing site A in 12 out of 25 males at 100 mg/kg and in 10 out of 25 males at 300 mg/kg. Additionally at dosing site B, the area was raised in 12 out of 25 males at 100 mg/kg and in 19 out of 25 males at 300 mg/kg. The raised areas had pale discoloration.
L1043: Similar to males, test article administration in females resulted in a raised area at dosing site A in 1 out of 25 females at 100 mg/kg and in 15 out of 25 females at 300 mg/kg. At dosing site B, the area was raised in 7 out of 25 females at 100 mg/kg and in 18 out of 25 females at 300 mg/kg. The raised areas had pale discoloration.
L1044: ## Body Weights
L1045: Animals were weighed once during predose, prior to dosing on day 1, and weekly thereafter. There were no test article related effects.
L1046: ## Feed Consumption
L1047: Food intake was recorded weekly. Any wet or spilled food was also noted. There were no test article related effects.
L1048: ## Gross Pathology
L1049: Animals were necropsied at the end of the study on day 183 via isoflurane inhalation.
L1050: There was a dose related increase in injection site reactions (raised area) for both injections sites A and B in males and females. This finding correlates to the pseudocyst finding noted during histopathology analysis.
L1051: All other findings were considering sporadic or incidental due to their low incidences, presence in dosed and control animals, or common in this animal model.

L1057: **Pseudocyst:** There was a dose dependent increase in males at 100 and 300 mg/kg only. In females there was a dose dependent increase across doses. This finding correlated with injection site reactions noted during gross pathology.
L1058: ## **Subcutaneous Injection site B:**
L1059: **Pseudocyst:** There was a dose dependent increase in males and females across doses. This finding correlated with injection site reactions noted during gross pathology.

L1061: There was one skin papilloma noted in a single female dosed 300 mg/kg that was terminated early due to its moribund condition at week 15. The sponsor stated this finding was within historical control. This finding is unlikely related to the test article because it was a single incidence and animals that reached their scheduled necropsy of 27 weeks did not have this finding.

L1083: Re: DDD Consult #2133: Lenacapavir (NDA 215973, NDA 215974)
L1084: Lenacapavir (LEN) is currently under review as an NME under two NDAs, 215973 [injectable (SC) (b) (4)] and 215974 (tablets). The proposed indication by the Applicant is (b) (4)
L1085: The Division of Dermatology and Dentistry was previously consulted because injection site reactions (ISRs) were the most common adverse reaction with lenacapavir subcutaneous injection. Based on preclinical histology in rats, rabbits and dogs these reactions were observed to be inflammatory granulomas. One of DAV's concerns was that injection site nodules and indurations can possibly last several weeks/months, and the longer-term safety data included in the resubmissions may help to further describe and understand injection site reactions associated with LEN.
L1086: DAV is requesting DDD'S review and assessment of the Applicant's Cumulative Review of Injection Site Reactions, including the Applicant's assessment of high pH formulations and ISRs. DAV requests any recommendations for communication of ISRs in labeling.
L1087: Additionally, per email dated July 18, 2022: DAV requests a review of Applicant's responses to FDA additional comments in complete response letters dated, February 28, 2022 (2.2.1 Comment 6).

L1093: ## **DDD Response:**
L1094: - Review and assessment of the Applicant's Cumulative Review of Injection Site Reactions, including the Applicant's assessment of high pH formulations and ISRs.Review and assessment of the Applicant's Cumulative Review of Injection Site Reactions (Focused on nodules and indurations):
L1095: Nodules and indurations were seen commonly across trials in the development program, affecting subjects in a fashion generally similar to that seen in the pivotal trial GS-US-200-4625 [nodules (25%), indurations (15%)]. Nodules and indurations generally persisted longer than other injection site reactions.
L1096: - Conclusion regarding the Applicant's assessment of high pH formulations: Review of the Applicant's presented nonclinical data for LEN, clinical data for LEN and clinical data of other approved ARVs does not identify a clear association between high formulation pH and duration of nodules and indurations.
- DDD reiterates that in ongoing or future trials, where possible, injection site nodules be followed to resolution or stabilization. In addition, DDD continues to recommend that human histopathology be obtained (e.g., punch biopsy in a few subjects). The presence of findings such as necrosis, hypersensitivity, granulomas, foreign bodies, fibrous tissue, etc. can aid in understanding the pathophysiology of nodule formation. This in turn can increase understanding of which treatments are most likely to be useful.
- Assessment of the extent to which glass particulate contamination, including sub-visible particles, may be associated with injection site nodules and indurations or other clinical effects.Information submitted (literature and nonclinical and clinical evidence from injectable ARVs) indicates that ISRs, including nodules and induration, most likely result from the presence of the drug depot rather than the potential presence of subvisible glass particulates in the closure system with borosilicate glass vials.
- Recommendations for communication of ISRs in labelingDDD agrees with DAV proposed edits to labeling for LEN in Section 6 of labeling.
- The Applicant's rationale to [REDACTED] (b) (4) is acceptable. The use of [REDACTED] (b) (4) to describe the duration of ISRs, nodules, and indurations is not recommended since it is not commonly used in clinical practice and not easily interpreted by prescribers. FDA proposes use of range [REDACTED] (b) (4). See also details of labeling communications.

L1131: ## **Clinical Histopathology**
L1132: The dermatologist assessments for two subjects who met the ISR criteria described above from trial GS-US-200-4625 included two biopsy reports, one for each of the two subjects.
L1133: For subject (b) (6), the dermatopathology report included 3 different injection sites (described clinically as smooth skin-colored papules, well-formed with assessment: rule
L1134: out foreign object (glass) vs injection site reaction) The report showed multinucleated foreign body-type giant cell reactions present within the deep dermis and subcutaneous space. No significant polarizable foreign body material was seen in the material sampled.
L1135: For subject (b) (6), the dermatopathology report included two sites (described clinically as nodules/irregular lesions with assessment: neoplasm of uncertain behavior rule out injection site reaction vs. foreign body). The report showed histochemical staining supporting the diagnosis of amyloidosis. The Investigator noted that the subject had received injections of enfuvirtide BID for more than 3 years. The amyloidosis was interpreted as possibly being secondary to injections with enfuvirtide. This supported by a report in the literature (Morilla 20091) of a case of localized amyloidosis associated with injection of enfuvirtide.
L1136: - It is observed that clinical histopathology received in the current submission includes one case (from trial GS-US-200-4625) demonstrating multinucleated foreign body-type giant cell reactions at injection sites.
L1137: ## Nonclinical Histopathology:
L1138: The Applicant notes that nonclinical studies of rats (TX-200-2014), rabbits (TX-200-2033) and dogs (TX-200-2047) showed microscopic findings of granulomatous inflammation at subcutaneous (SC) injection sites. The Applicant notes further that granulomatous inflammation has been observed after SC and intramuscular implantation of bioactive material, including those for HIV treatment and concludes that inflammation and foreign body response to the lenacapavir (LEN) SC depot is an expected host response. (IR response received 9/23/2021, p. 12)
L1139: ## Discussion of Injection Site Reactions/Nodules:
L1140: There was no standardized definition of nodule or induration provided to Investigators for the pivotal clinical trial, GS-US-200-4625 or for the supportive trial, GS-US-200-4334.
L1141: The Applicant, however, included the following definitions of induration and nodule in Injection site manuals for the Phase 1 trials: GS-US-4070, GS-US-200-4538. (IR response received 10/26/2021, pp. 41/65 and 49/65)
L1142: **Induration:** (Palpable thickening, firmness, or hardening of soft tissue). Usually well demarcated with palpable borders, can be visible (raised or sunken compared to surrounding skin), is often 'woody' to touch and has a flat shape (versus the rounder shape of a nodule); it can best be described by palpation.2
L1143: **Nodule:** Discrete or well-demarcated soft tissue mass or lump that is firm.3

L1148: ## Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine2
L1149: **Nodule:** A larger (0.5–5.0 cm), firm lesion raised above the surface of the surrounding skin. This differs from a papule only in size (e.g., a large dermal nevomelanocytic nevus).
L1150: **Papule:** A small, solid lesion, &lt;0.5 cm in diameter, raised above the surface of the surrounding skin and thus palpable (e.g., a closed comedone, or whitehead, in acne).
L1151: ## Bologna, Jean, L. et al. Dermatology3
L1152: ## **Nodule**
L1153: - Palpable, circumscribed
- Larger volume than papule, usually &gt;1 cm in diameter
- Involves the dermis and/or the subcutis
- Greatest portion may be beneath the skin surface or exophytic
L1154: ## **Papule**
L1155: - Elevated (palpable), circumscribed
- &lt;1 cm in diameter
- Elevation due to increased thickness of the epidermis and/or cells or deposits within the dermis
- May have secondary changes (e.g., scale, crust)
- The profile can be flat-topped (lichenoid), dome-shaped, umbilicated, or verrucous
L1156: ## Fitzpatrick's Dermatology4
L1157: ## **Nodule**
L1158: A nodule is a palpable lesion greater than 1 cm with a domed, spherical or ovoid shape. They may be solid or cystic. Depending on the anatomic component(s) primarily involved, nodules are of 5 main types: (1) epidermal, (2) epidermal–dermal, (3) dermal, (4) dermal–subdermal, and (5)

Texture is an important additional feature of nodules: firm, soft, boggy, fluctuant, etc. Similarly, different surfaces of nodules, such as smooth, keratotic, ulcerated, or fungating, also help direct diagnostic considerations. *Tumor*, also sometimes included under the heading of nodule, may be used to describe a more irregularly shaped mass, benign or malignant.
L1166: ## Papule
L1167: A papule is an elevated or depressed lesion less than 1 cm in size, which may be solid or cystic. Among other characteristics, papules may be further described by their topography. Some examples include papules that are sessile, pedunculated, dome-shaped, flat-topped, filiform, mamillated, acuminated (conical), or umbilicated.
L1168: ## ➤ **Regarding the current NDAs under review: 215973, 215974**
L1169: The primary study that supports the safety and efficacy of LEN is the Phase 2/3 study in HTE (heavily treatment experienced) people with HIV (PWH) (Study GS-US-200-4625), which is further supported by a Phase 2 study of LEN in treatment-naive PWH (Study GS-US-200-4334).
L1170: Supportive safety data are also provided from 2 Phase 1 studies in healthy participants (Studies GS-US-200-4538 and GS-US-200-5709); these Phase 1 studies also contributed to the characterization of the pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles of LEN and its metabolites, supporting the clinical pharmacology of LEN and the dosing interval.
L1171: The primary data (for establishing safety and efficacy) is based on 26-week data from **GS-US-200-4625** (CAPELLA), described by the Applicant as a “partially randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind multicenter trial.” The proposed indication, as of the time of this consult (11/17/22 – labeling sent to applicant 11/04/2022), is “the treatment of (HIV-1) infection in heavily treatment experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.”
L1172: ## Study Endpoints:
L1173: The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects in Cohort 1 achieving \ge 0.5 \log_{10} copies/mL reduction from baseline in HIV-1 RNA at the end of the functional monotherapy period.
L1174: The secondary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of participants in Cohort 1 with plasma HIV-1 RNA &lt; 50 copies/mL and &lt; 200 copies/mL at Weeks 26 and 52 of treatment based on the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-defined snapshot algorithm

L1176: ## **Study Design Schema**
L1177: This trial design shows that there is no arm where active injected drug is compared with placebo injected drug. There are two enrolled cohorts: Cohort 1, if subjects had a &lt; 0.5 \log_{10} HIV-1 RNA decline compared to the screening visit and Cohort 2, if subjects had a \ge 0.5 \log_{10} HIV-1 RNA decline compared to the screening visit or after Cohort 1 reached its planned sample size. Regarding Cohort 1, in the 14-day functional monotherapy period, subjects in Cohort 1 were randomized in a 2:1 ratio in a blinded fashion to receive either drug product or placebo, while continuing their failing regimen.
L1178: - **Cohort 1A** subjects received subcutaneous (SC) LEN on day 1 SC (14 days after 1st dose of oral LEN) and once every 6 months (26 weeks). Also initiate their OBR
- **Cohort 1B** subjects received placebo for 14 days, then oral LEN for and initiate their OBR on Day 15, then SC LEN at Day 1 SC (14 days after 1st dose of oral LEN and 28 days into trial) and once every 6 months (26 weeks).
- **Cohort 2:** received oral LEN for 14 days, then SC LEN at Day 1 SC (14 days after 1st dose of oral LEN) and once every 6 months (26 weeks).

L1198: ## 1.5 mL Injection Preparation and Administration Instructions:
L1199: 13. With one hand, pinch a fold of skin where the injection is to be given. The initial injection should be given in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen. If a subject has a tattoo or scar in the right lower quadrant, another quadrant may be used. For the second injection, rotate injection site clockwise, ensuring the subsequent injection is at least 4 inches away from the previous injection site. For additional injections, rotate injection sites clockwise, ensuring subsequent injections are at least 4 inches away from the other injection site(s). The injection site location(s) should be noted in the source documents.

L1285: ## ► **Review of Applicant's Responses to FDA Additional Comments in Complete Response Letters dated February 28, 2022: 2.2.1 Clinical Comment 6**
L1286: The Applicant states that information submitted (literature and nonclinical and clinical evidence from injectable ARVs) support the position that ISRs, including nodules and induration, most likely result from the presence of the drug depot rather than the potential presence of subvisible glass particulates in the closure system with borosilicate glass vials.

L1288: ## ► **Applicant's assessment of injection site reactions in "Cumulative Review of Injection Site Reactions" (Seq 0015, m1.11.3, Section 2.2, p 62)**
L1289: The Applicant states that: "Given the majority of ISRs are of low grade, rarely lead to discontinuation, and frequently resolve over a short period of time, the benefit:risk of LEN remains favorable and consistent with Gilead's overall assessment of ISRs previously provided to the Agency (Seq 0015, m1.11.3, Section 2.2)." (Response to IR of 10/12/2021 received 10/26/202, pp. 11, 12). **See below for Applicant's previously provided overall assessment:**
L1290: "To summarize, we have conducted a comprehensive assessment of injection site reactions (ISRs) across the LEN program, including detailed review of individual cases with the investigators. Our overall assessment is as follows. In Studies GS-US-200-4625 and GS-US-200-4334, approximately half or fewer of the participants (55.6% and 38.8%, respectively) experienced at least 1 AEs of LEN-related ISRs, which were mostly non-serious, Grade 1 or 2, and rarely led to study drug discontinuation. Most AEs of ISRs resolved within days, but those of induration and nodules lasted longer (as described in Gilead's previous response, Seq 0008). These AEs of induration or nodules were generally small (less than a few centimeters), not visible to the participant or the investigator, not causing persistent discomfort to participants, and only detectable upon deep palpation. There were rarely any gross inflammatory components, such as tenderness or erythema, to these AEs of induration or nodules, and when there was coincident pain or erythema, they resolved quickly. There were no reports of tissue destruction (e.g., necrosis), or, upon careful review, suggestion of other more serious reactions such as sterile abscess or persistent tissue damage. No participants appeared to have any safety signal suggesting that LEN was being administered into a deeper tissue than the intended subcutaneous space (e.g., muscle). In written, verbal, and video communication with investigators who took care of participants with AEs of persistent induration or nodule, none were concerned with any potential long term permanent adverse effect, none felt the AEs required additional consultation (e.g., with a dermatologist), and all agreed that those AEs were resolving slowly over time. In general investigators commented on the benign nature of nodules, with some noting that nodules might be more visible in a person who is lean and self-conscious of body image."
L1291: ## **Nodules:**
L1292: "Based on the totality of Gilead's nonclinical assessment, the induration or nodules after SC LEN injection appears to be a normal and expected tissue body response, manifesting as chronic granulomatous inflammation histologically, to a foreign body (i.e., a drug depot)
L1293: without permanent adverse effect. We have not found evidence of injection site nodules or induration being reflective of more serious complications, or resulting from aberrant injections, nor have we found evidence that nodules are related to body habitus or immunologic status.... In summary, our assessment is that nodules that rise to the level of AE reporting occur in a subset of individuals receiving LEN, represent subcutaneous deposition of the drug itself and expected tissue reaction, and are not associated with adverse clinical or pharmacologic consequences."
L1294: ► This reviewer finds the Applicant's assessment, especially as it relates to injection site nodules and indurations, reasonable.

L1324: ## **Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience**
L1325: ## **Injection-Associated Adverse Reactions**
L1326: *Local Injection Site Reactions (ISRs):* The most frequent adverse reactions associated with the intramuscular administration of CABENUVA were ISRs. After 14,682 injections, 3,663 ISRs were reported. One percent (1%) of subjects discontinued treatment with CABENUVA because of ISRs. Most ISRs were mild (Grade 1, 75%) or moderate (Grade 2, 36%). Four percent (4%) of subjects experienced severe (Grade 3) ISRs, and no subjects experienced Grade 4 ISRs. The most commonly reported ISR was localized pain/discomfort (79%) regardless of severity or relatedness. Other manifestations of ISRs reported in more than 1% of subjects over the duration of the analysis period included **nodules (14%)***, induration (12%), swelling (8%), erythema (4%), pruritus (4%), bruising (3%), warmth (2%), and hematoma (2%). Abscess and cellulitis at the injection site were each reported in less than 1% of subjects. The median duration of ISR events was 3 days.

L1418: ## ➤ **Comments Regarding the Effects of Formulation pH:**
L1419: The question arises whether high pH could be contributing to long duration of indurations and nodules.
L1420: The applicant's assessment of high pH formulations and ISRs: submitted in module 5.3.5.3 in the submission dated 6, 27, 2022 (SDN#38) includes:

- Clinical Data of Other Approved antiretrovirals (ARVs):
L1422: ## **Nonclinical Data for LEN**
L1423: The applicant describes a number of non-clinical studies regarding the effect of pH on chronic granulomatous inflammation and foreign body response at the SC injection sites.
L1424: • A single-dose SC injection local tolerance study (TX-200-2019) of LEN using a solution of LEN free acid (approximately pH 7) and LEN sodium (approximately pH 9.5) was conducted in rabbits. Edema correlated with macroscopic observation of thickening at the injection site and microscopic observation of granulomatous inflammation were observed on Day 92. The macroscopic and microscopic findings did not differ between the different LEN formulations (approximately pH 7 or approximately pH 9.5). The granulomatous inflammation decreased in incidence and/or severity by Day 183 and Day 274, suggestive of a process of maturation or recovery.
L1425: • A single- (Day 1) and second-dose (Day 1 and Day 92) SC injection toxicity study with a 13-week observation period (TX-200-2014) of LEN using a solution of LEN free acid (approximately pH 7.0) and LEN sodium (approximately pH 9.5) was conducted in rats. LEN-related edema (very slight to moderate), macroscopic thickening and/or tan discoloration, correlative granulomatous inflammation (minimal to moderate; with or without necrosis), and macrophage infiltrate were present at the SC injection sites of animals administered either formulation of LEN (approximately pH 7 and approximately pH 9.5). Evidence of LEN-related granulomatous inflammation reversibility included decreased severity relative to SC injection site(s) used more recently, and/or resolution to a minimal macrophage infiltrate.
L1426: • A 9-month (once monthly) SC injection toxicity study (TX-200-2017) of LEN using a solution of LEN free acid (approximately pH 7.0) and LEN sodium (approximately pH 9.5) was conducted in dogs. Lenacapavir-related microscopic observations of necrosis, granulomatous
L1427: inflammation, mixed cell inflammation, and/or macrophage infiltrate were observed at the SC injection sites of animals administered either formulation of LEN (approximately pH 7.0 and approximately pH 9.5). At each sacrifice interval, granulomatous inflammation, with variable central necrosis, was generally observed in all but the last site dosed and was considered indicative of the maturation/recovery process. In the oldest injection sites, inflammation had recovered to a macrophage infiltrate in some animals. Overall, an increased interval since dosing was generally associated with a successive decrease in the overall incidence/severity of microscopic findings.
L1428: • A SC injection local tolerance study (TX-200-2033) of LEN using a solution of LEN free acid (pH 7.1) and LEN sodium (pH 9.4) was conducted in rabbits. On Day 4, LEN-related microscopic findings at the injection site consisted of slight to marked necrosis, minimal to moderate mixed cell inflammation, and minimal to slight mononuclear cell infiltrates, that correlated with the macroscopic observation of thickening in all animals administered LEN with either formulation (pH 7.1 and pH 9.4). On Day 29, LEN-related microscopic findings of marked granulomatous inflammation and slight to marked necrosis correlated with the macroscopic observation of thickening in all animals administered LEN. Overall, the incidence and severity of mixed cell and/or granulomatous inflammation and necrosis were similar between dose levels and formulations, regardless of pH. LEN-related edema correlated with the macroscopic observation of thickening and the microscopic observations of mixed cell or granulomatous inflammation, necrosis, and mononuclear cell infiltrates at the SC injection site of animals administered LEN.
L1429: •A SC injection local tolerance study (TX-200-2010) of LEN (LEN was suspended in vehicle (b) (4) pH 7.4) was conducted in rabbits (NDA 215973, Seq 0001, m4.2.3.6). Lenacapavir-related dermal observations of very slight edema, very slight to well-defined erythema, and desquamation were noted on Day 4; these findings were resolved by Day 29. These observations were minor and recovered by the end of the study; therefore, they were considered not adverse. On Day 4, LEN-related microscopic findings included slight or marked granulomatous inflammation of the subcutis and slight to moderate granulomatous inflammation of the dermis. SC granulomatous inflammation correlated with the macroscopic observation of white discoloration. On Day 29, LEN-related findings of minimal to moderate granulomatous inflammation of the subcutis and was correlated with the macroscopic observation of white discolorations. Minimal mixed cell infiltrates of the dermis were present. No granulomatous inflammation of the dermis was present, indicating reversal.
L1430: ## **Non-clinical conclusion:**
L1431: The Applicant states that their available nonclinical data suggest that chronic granulomatous inflammation and foreign body response at the SC injection site are expected to occur for any antiretroviral compound including LEN due to the presence of a SC drug depot, and irrespective of the pH of the formulation.
L1432: This reviewer agrees this is a reasonable conclusion.
L1433: ## **Clinical Data for LEN:**
L1434: ## **From Applicant presented information:**
L1435: The same SC formulation of LEN 309 mg/mL (2 x 1.5 mL injection – 927mg, initial (pH = 9.0 to 10.0)) was used in a total of 219 participants across a Phase 1 study in healthy participants (Study GS-US-200-5709, n = 44), a Phase 2 study in treatment-naive PWH (Study GS-US-200-4334, n = 103) and a Phase 2/3 study in heavily treatment-experienced PWH with multidrug resistance (Study GS-US-200-4625, n = 72).
L1436: Most AEs of ISRs resolved within days, but those of indurations and nodules lasted longer (median [Q1, Q3]: for resolved = 70 [15, 196] and 148 [70, 307] days in Study GS-US-200-4625, for resolved = 278 [136, 366] and 202 [101, 213] days in Study GS-US-200-4334, and for resolved = 27 [15, 127] and 421 [113, 421] in Study GS-US-200-5709, respectively). There were rarely any gross inflammatory components, such as tenderness or erythema, to these AEs of indurations or nodules, and when there was coincident pain or erythema, they resolved quickly. Investigators treating participants with AEs of persistent indurations or nodules reported that those AEs were resolving slowly over time. In general, investigators commented on the benign nature of the nodules.
L1437: A SC aqueous formulation of LEN free acid suspension (pH 7.1) was used in a total of 61 participants in one Phase 1 trial in healthy participants (Study GS-US-200-4070, n = 32), and a Phase 1b proof-of-concept trial in treatment-naive PWH (Study GS-US-200-4072, n = 29). In trial GS-US-200-4070, single doses 30 mg, 100mg, 300mg, and 450 mg were examined. In trial GS-US-200-4072, single doses 150mg, 50 mg, 20 mg, and multiple doses 450 mg, and 750 mg were examined.
L1438: Nodules and indurations were reported in 28.1% and 25.0% of participants in Study GS-US-200-4070, and 20.7% and 24.1% of participants in Study GS-US-200-4072, respectively. Median (Q1, Q3) duration (days) of resolved indurations and nodules was 4 (2, 12), 51 (7, 169) in Study GS-US-200-4070 and 7 (6, 45), 49 (4, 225) in Study GS-US-200-4072.
L1439: ## **Clinical conclusion:**
L1440: Regarding nodules and indurations, the data from the trials described above is suggestive that nodules and indurations persist longer in the trials with initially higher pH (initial pH = 9.0 to 10.0). However, doses examined in the lower pH trials were generally lower than those examined in the higher pH trials. Additionally, the number of subjects (sample size) in the lower pH trials is smaller, 61 versus 219, for the higher pH trials. It is noted also that non-clinical findings presented by the applicant do not show a significant pH effect.
L1441: ## **Clinical Data of Other Approved ARVs:**
L1442: The Applicant notes that other approved ARVs for SC or intramuscular (IM) injections have been associated with similar or greater incidence of ISRs.
L1443: ## • Approved labeling **CABENUVA (cabotegravir extended-release injectable suspension; rilpivirine extended-release injectable suspension)** 1/2021: **Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience**
L1444: “The most commonly reported ISR was localized pain/discomfort (79%) regardless of severity or relatedness. Other manifestations of ISR’s reported in more than 1% of subjects over the duration of the analysis period included *nodules* (14%), *induration* (12%), swelling (8%), erythema (4%), pruritus (4%), bruising (3%), warmth (2%), and hematoma (2%).”
L1445: ## • Approved labeling **FUZEON (enfuvirtide)** 8/2019: **Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience**
L1446: “The majority of ISRs were associated with erythema, induration, the presence of nodules or cysts, and mild to moderate pain at the injection site (Table 2)”: pain/discomfort (96%), *induration* (90%), erythema (91%), *nodules and cysts* (80%), pruritus (65%), and ecchymosis (52%), including participants with Grade 3 or 4 ISRs.
L1447: ## **Data for Other SC Administered Alkaline Products**

L1458: Pertinent information provided by the applicant includes a study (Dorris1) wherein dogs were randomized to control (with in-line filtration) and experimental (without in-line filtration) groups and received concentrated solutions of particles. L1460: ## • **Non-clinical data for LEN and other ARVs:**
L1461: A single-dose SC injection local tolerance study (Gilead Sciences: TX-200-2019) of LEN in rabbits was conducted using LEN formulations which were pharmacy compounded at the site (b)(4), and therefore were not expected to contain any intrinsic glass particulates resulting from an interaction between the LEN injection formulation and the borosilicate glass vials. Non-adverse edema correlated with macroscopic observation of thickening at the injection site and microscopic observation of granulomatous inflammation observed on Day 92. The granulomatous inflammation decreased in incidence and/or severity by Day 183 and Day 274, indicative of the maturation/recovery process.

L1472: The Applicant concludes that the available non-clinical data from local tolerance studies of ARV agents presented above suggest that chronic granulomatous inflammation and foreign body response at the injection site (SC or IM) occurs due to the drug depot of the product and is independent of glass particulates.

L1474: ## **• Assessment of ISRs from clinical studies of LEN and other ARVs:**
L1475: According to the applicant, preliminary data from an ongoing Phase 1 Study GS-US-200-5710 (titled, "A Phase 1 Study in Healthy Participant to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Subcutaneous and Intramuscular Lenacapavir") provides some indication of the extent to which ISRs are independent of glass particulates. In this study, the LEN injection formulations used are not expected to contain any intrinsic glass particles resulting from interaction of LEN injection formulation with borosilicate glass vials because the formulations are pharmacy compounded at the clinical site (b) (4). The applicant notes that participants receiving SC LEN in the study experienced ISRs of similar type, severity, and duration as in Studies GS-US-200-4625 and GS-US-200-4334. The applicant states that these data suggest that the subvisible glass particles are not directly causing nor affecting the ISRs, which are most likely occurring due to the presence of SC LEN depot.
L1476: It is noted that other approved ARVs for SC or IM injections have been associated with similar or greater incidence and severity of nodules and induration. Following IM administration of cabotegravir, nodules and indurations were reported in 14% and 12% of patients, respectively. Following SC administration of FUZEON (enfuvirtide), induration and nodules and cysts, were reported in 90% and 80% of patients, respectively.

- Approved labeling FUZEON (enfuvirtide) 8/2019: Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience
L1478: ## **General Conclusion:**
L1479: The Applicant states that information submitted (literature and nonclinical and clinical evidence from injectable ARVs) support the position that ISRs, including nodules and induration, most likely result from the presence of the drug depot rather than the potential presence of subvisible glass particulates in the closure system with borosilicate glass vials.

L1502: ## 1. Background
L1503: In this submission, the sponsor included a carcinogenicity study report in mice. This study was intended to assess the carcinogenic potential of Sunlenca (Lenacapavir): GS-6207(b)(4) (Na salt, hereafter referred to as GS-6207) when administered once every 13 weeks by subcutaneous injection (total of 2 doses) to 001178-T (hemizygous) RasH2 mice, with a 13-week observation period following each dose. Results of this review have been discussed with the reviewing pharmacologist Dr. Diggs.
L1504: In this review, the phrase "dose response relationship" (trend) refers to the linear component of the effect of treatment, and not necessarily to a strictly increasing or decreasing mortality or tumor incidence rate as dose increases.
L1505: ## 2. Mouse Study
L1506: Two separate experiments were conducted, one in male mice and one in female mice. In each of these two experiments there were three treated groups, one vehicle control group, and one positive control group. One hundred and ten rasH2 transgenic mice of each sex were assigned randomly to one of the five groups by a stratified randomization scheme designed to achieve similar group mean body weights in equal size of 25 animals except the positive control group which had 10 animals. The dose levels for the three treated groups were at 30, 100, or 300 mg/kg/dose, respectively, via SC injection once every 13 weeks (total of 2 doses), for both males and females, as indicated in Table 1. In this review, these dose groups would be referred to as the low, medium, and high dose group, respectively. The positive control group was administered with one intraperitoneal dose of 75 mg/kg N-methyl-N-nitrosourea on Day 1 of the dosing phase. This group was included to verify sensitivity of the test system to detect carcinogenicity effect. The vehicle control group received (b)(6)% w/w polyethylene glycol 300 and (b)(4)% w/w sterile water for injection and were administered in the same manner as the treated groups.
L1507: **Table 1: Experimental Design in Mouse Study**

L1509: Animals in group 5 were dosed with one intraperitoneal dose of positive control article on Day 1 of the dosing phase.
L1510: Group 1, 2, 3, and 4, were dosed via SC injection once every 13 weeks (total of 2 doses)
L1511: During the administration period, all animals were checked for morbidity, mortality, injury, twice daily (a.m. and p.m.), abnormal findings were recorded for toxicity animals as they were observed. Cage side observations were conducted for each carcinogenicity animal once daily during the dosing phase, except on days when detailed observations were conducted. The animals were removed from the cage, and detailed observations were conducted for each animal once during the pre-dose phase, on Day 1, and weekly (based on Day 1) thereafter to Week 26, and on Day 182 of the dosing phase. Detailed observations were also collected for each carcinogenicity animal on the day of scheduled sacrifice (Day 183, only those animals scheduled for sacrifice on that day). Abnormal findings or an indication of normal was recorded. Detailed examinations for palpable masses were done weekly, the time of onset, location, size, appearance, and progression of each grossly visible or palpable mass, observed in
L1512: carcinogenicity mice, were recorded, any animal showing signs of severe debility or intoxication, and if determined to be moribund or suffering excessively was euthanized. Observations included, but will not be limited to, evaluation for reaction to treatment. Histopathological examinations were performed on all animals found dead or killed moribund or sacrificed at the end of the experiment. Body weights were recorded for carcinogenicity animals once during the predose phase, before dosing on Day 1, and weekly (based on Day 1) thereafter to Week 26 and on Day 182.
L1513: ## 2.1. Sponsor's analyses
L1514: ## 2.1.1. Survival analysis
L1515: In the sponsor's analysis, the tests for survival comparisons were performed with a two-sided risk for increasing and decreasing mortality with dose. Tests were performed for dose response and for each dosed group against control using Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimates, along with log-rank and Wilcoxon tests. These were performed using LIFETEST procedure in SAS. The time to death or sacrifice (in weeks) was the dependent variable. Treatment group was included as the strata. Animals with a death or sacrifice status recorded as a planned sacrifice (interim or terminal) or an accidental death were censored in the analysis.
L1516: ## Sponsor's findings:
L1517: Sponsor's analysis showed the numbers of mice surviving to their terminal necropsy were 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 19 (76%), 23 (92%), and 3 (30%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in male mice, respectively, and 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 21 (84%), 22 (88%), and 4 (40%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in females, respectively. The sponsor's report concluded that, there were statistically significant higher mortality in the medium dose group, when compared to the vehicle control group in male mice (p-value = 0.0423 for the Log-Rank test and P = 0.0409 for the Wilcoxon test.).
L1518: ## 2.1.2. Tumor data analysis
L1519: In the sponsor's analysis, tests to compare tumor incidence were performed, with a one-sided risk for increasing or decreasing incidence with dose. Tests were performed for dose response and for each dosed group against the vehicle control group. Occult or non-palpable and fatal tumors were analyzed by the IARC asymptotic fixed interval-based prevalence test and death-rate test (Peto et al., 1980). The cut-off points for the interval-based test were Weeks 1 to 13, 14 to before terminal sacrifice, and the terminal sacrifice. Actual target dose levels were used as the scores for all groups. Fatal and non-fatal tumors were analyzed together, with separate stratum for each. Tumors of uncertain context were included in the analysis as non-fatal. The test was implemented using PROC MULTTEST in the SAS system (SAS, 2008). In the case of sparse tables (&lt;10 total tumor bearing animals across the groups analyzed for the trend or pairwise test), the exact form of the test was used. Otherwise, the asymptotic version of the test was used. For each given tumor type, a statistical analysis was performed if the incidence in at least one dosed group was increased by at least two occurrences over the vehicle control group.
L1520: Observable or palpable (superficial as in mammary or skin) tumors were analyzed using the methods previously described for analyzing survival (on-set rate method described in Peto et al., 1980), using the time to death or time of detection of the tumor (in weeks) as a surrogate for the tumor onset time.
L1521: ## **Adjustment for the multiplicity:**
L1522: For multiplicity adjustment testing, the sponsor did not present any adjustment, unadjusted P-values were reported, and statistically significant results are given at the 5% level.
L1523: ## **Sponsor's findings:**
L1524: The sponsor's analysis showed statistically significant increasing dose response relationships at the 5% level, for the incidence of benign papilloma, squamous cell in skin/subcutis in female mice (p-value = 0.0498 for the Log-Rank test and P = 0.0498 for the Wilcoxon test.).
L1525: ## 2.2 Reviewer's analyses
L1526: To verify sponsor's analysis and to perform additional analyses suggested by the reviewing pharmacologist, this reviewer independently performed the survival and tumor data analyses. Data used in this reviewer's analyses were provided by the sponsor electronically on June 27, 2022, via SN0038.
L1527: ## 2.2.1 Survival analysis
L1528: In the reviewer's analysis, intercurrent mortality data were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier product limit method. The Kaplan-Meier's curves were presented graphically for male and female mice separately. The dose response relationship and homogeneity of survival distributions were tested for the treatment groups using the Likelihood Ratio test and the Log-Rank test. The intercurrent mortality data are given in Tables 1A and 1B in the appendix for male and female mice, respectively. The Kaplan-Meier curves for survival rate are given in Figures 1A and 1B in the appendix for male and female mice, respectively. Results of the tests for dose response relationship and homogeneity of survivals, are given in Tables 2A and 2B in the appendix for male and female mice, respectively.
L1529: ## **Reviewer's findings:**
L1530: This reviewer's analysis showed the numbers of mice surviving to their terminal necropsy were 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 19 (76%), 23 (92%), and 3 (30%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in male mice, respectively, and 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 21 (84%), 22 (88%), and 4 (40%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in females, respectively. The reviewer's report showed no statistically significant dose response relationship in the mortality of both male and female mice. The pairwise comparisons showed a statistically significant increase in mortality between the medium dose group and the vehicle control group in male mice (p-value = 0.0343).
L1531: ## 2.2.2. Tumor data analysis
L1532: In the reviewer's analysis, the tumor data were analyzed for dose response relationship across vehicle control group and the treated groups, as well as the pairwise comparisons of vehicle control group with each of the treated groups using the Poly-k method described in the paper of Bailer and Portier (1988) and Bieler and Williams (1993). In this method, an animal that lives the full study period (w_{max}) or dies before the terminal sacrifice with development of the tumor type being tested gets a score of s_h = 1. An animal that dies at Week w_h without development of the given tumor type before the end of the study gets a score of
L1533: s_h = \left( \frac{w_h}{w_{\max}} \right)^k &lt; 1. The adjusted group size is defined as \Sigma s_h. As an interpretation, an animal with score
L1534: s_h = 1 can be considered as a whole animal, while an animal with score s_h &lt; 1 can be considered as a partial animal. The adjusted group size \Sigma s_h is equal to N (the original group size) if all animals live up to the end of the study or if each animal develops the given tumor being tested, otherwise the adjusted group size is less than N. These adjusted group sizes are then used for the dose response relationship (or the pairwise comparison) tests using the Cochran-Armitage test. One critical point for Poly-k test is the choice of the appropriate value of k. For long term 104-week standard rat study, a value of k=3 is suggested in the literature [Gebregziabher and Hoel (2009), Moon et al. (2003), Portier, et al. (1986)]. Hence, this reviewer used k=3 for the analysis of the data. Based on the intent to treat (ITT) principle W_{\max} was considered as 105 for both male and female mice.
L1535: For the calculation of p-values, if there were less than 10 tumors bearing animals across all treatment groups for a given tumor type, the exact tests based on the discrete permutation distribution were used, with dose levels (0, 30, 100, and 300 for male mice and female mice) as scores, and asymptotic tests were used for tumor types with higher incidences. The tumor rates and the p-values of the tested tumor types are listed in Tables 3A and 3B in the appendix for male mice and female mice, respectively.
L1536: ## Multiple testing adjustments:
L1537: Following the FDA more recently revised draft guidance for the carcinogenicity study design and data analysis, for the 26 weeks mouse study this reviewer used significance levels of 0.05 for common and rare tumors, for dose response relationship (trend) tests and for pairwise comparisons.
L1538: A tumor is defined as a rare tumor if the published spontaneous rate or the spontaneous rate of the vehicle control of the tumor is less than 1%, and a common tumor is defined as one with tumor rate greater than or equal to 1%.
L1539: ## Reviewer's findings:
L1540: Following the multiple testing adjustment method described above, this reviewer's analysis showed no tumor types with a statistically significant dose response relationship in tumor incidences with increased Sunlenca (Lenacapavir) dose in both male and female mice. The pairwise comparisons test also showed no statistically significant increases in tumor incidences in any groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice.
L1541: The pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the incidences of malignant lymphoma in hematolymphoid system, benign papilloma, squamous cell in the skin/subcutis, benign papilloma, squamous cell in stomach nonglandular, when compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice (p-values &lt;0.0001, =0.0010, =0.0010, for males, and &lt;0.0001, =0.0002, =0.0002, for females, respectively). Also, the pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the incidences of malignant carcinoma, Squamous Cell in stomach nonglandular in male mice, (p-values =0.0423).
L1542: ## 3. Summary
L1543: In this submission, the sponsor included a carcinogenicity study report in mice. This study was intended to assess the carcinogenic potential of Sunlenca (Lenacapavir): GS-6207(b)(4) (Na salt, hereafter referred to as
L1544: GS-6207) when administered once every 13 weeks by subcutaneous injection (total of 2 doses) to 001178-T (hemizygous) RasH2 mice, with a 13-week observation period following each dose.
L1545: ## Mouse Study:
L1546: In this study two separate experiments were conducted, one in male mice and one in female mice. In each of these two experiments there were three treated groups, one vehicle control group, and one positive control group. One hundred and ten rasH2 transgenic mice of each sex were assigned randomly to one of the five groups by a stratified randomization scheme designed to achieve similar group mean body weights in equal size of 25 animals except the positive control group which had 10 animals. The dose levels for the three treated groups were at 30, 100, or 300 mg/kg/dose, respectively, via SC injection once every 13 weeks (total of 2 doses), for both males and females, as indicated in Table 1. In this review, these dose groups would be referred to as the low, medium, and high dose group, respectively. The positive control group was administered with one intraperitoneal dose of 75 mg/kg N-methyl-N-nitrosourea on Day 1 of the dosing phase. This group was included to verify sensitivity of the test system to detect carcinogenicity effect. The vehicle control group received (b)(6) % w/w polyethylene glycol 300 and (b)(4) % w/w sterile water for injection, were administered in the same manner as the treated groups.
L1547: This reviewer's analysis showed the numbers of mice surviving to their terminal necropsy were 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 19 (76%), 23 (92%), and 3 (30%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in male mice, respectively, and 24 (96%), 24 (96%), 21 (84%), 22 (88%), and 4 (40%) in the vehicle control, low, medium, high, and positive control groups, in females, respectively. The reviewer's report showed no statistically significant dose response relationship in the mortality of both male and female mice. The pairwise comparisons showed a statistically significant increase in mortality between the medium dose group and the vehicle control group in male mice (p-value = 0.0343).
L1548: For tumor data, following the multiple testing adjustment method described above, this reviewer's analysis showed no tumor types with a statistically significant dose response relationship in tumor incidences with increased Sunlenca (Lenacapavir) dose in both male and female mice. The pairwise comparisons test also showed no statistically significant increases in tumor incidences in any groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice.
L1549: The pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the incidences of malignant lymphoma in hematolymphoid system, benign papilloma, squamous cell in the skin/subcutis, benign papilloma, squamous cell in stomach nonglandular, when compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice (p-values &lt;0.0001, =0.0010, =0.0010, for males, and &lt;0.0001, =0.0002, =0.0002, for females, respectively). Also, the pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the incidences of malignant carcinoma, Squamous Cell in stomach nonglandular in male mice, (p-values =0.0423).
